pr.title: Show and address an unnamed agent session by the last group of its ID
pr.head: e3decc1d8982361103b6a25b653f6926f0412eda

summary: Projector lets agent sessions find and message one another. An unnamed session needs a display label so you can tell which session sent or received a message.

Codex uses time-ordered session IDs. Their first eight characters can match for sessions started close together. This change displays the final 12-character group instead, through one shared helper. You can send to that short ID in either case; a name or full ID takes precedence, and an ambiguous short ID is refused.

cards.title: Review validation
cards.html:
• The configured gate and exact-head CI passed.
  • All 48 focused agent and relay lifecycle tests passed on Python 3.12.5.
  • The earlier full review reproduced an existing keychain test error at the merge base on Python 3.15.2. That test remains unchanged.

groups.title: Use one stable label for unnamed sessions
groups.kicker: Display a random session-ID suffix wherever an agent is named
intro: A session ID is the full value that identifies an agent conversation. Its display label is shorter. short_id takes the last UUID group, or the last 12 characters of another ID, without consulting other sessions.
The shared label logic reaches list and registration output, message previews, read headers, send confirmations, and errors. Messages keep their full sender IDs, so stored messages need no migration.

files.note: Centralizes suffix labels and applies them to sender displays.

checks.text: Traced every label caller: names still win in display output, while JSON and stored messages retain full session IDs.
Traced name/full-ID precedence and reply handling, then ran local and relay regressions. Short-ID collisions refuse before message or event files are written.

groups.title: Resolve short IDs before sending a message
groups.kicker: Keep name and full-ID precedence, and refuse ambiguous suffixes
intro: When you send a new message, Projector now tries the recipient’s name, full session ID, and short ID in that order. Short-ID matching ignores case. The existing recipient checks still require one live session signed in to the same GitHub login.
When two eligible live sessions share a short ID, the command lists both full IDs and writes no message. Replies use the original sender’s full ID and never fall back to a short-ID match.

files.note: Adds short IDs to the recipient argument’s help text.

checks.text: Read the agent command parser and dispatch together: the argument reaches the shared send implementation without a separate lookup path.

groups.title: Keep display labels distinct and consistent
groups.kicker: Exercise stable labels, recipient precedence, ambiguity, and relay delivery
intro: The tests create two Codex sessions with the same time prefix and check that their display labels differ. They also check that previews agree with later list and read output.

The added routing regressions send through lowercase and uppercase short IDs, preserve name precedence, refuse ambiguous or lapsed recipients without writing state, and deliver a message to a session on another machine.

files.note: Tests stable labels and short-ID recipient selection through the CLI.

checks.text: Ran the agent tests and relay lifecycle tests with Python 3.12.5: 48 passed.

files.note: Adds delivery through a remote session’s short ID and retains generated-summary checks.

checks.text: The unchanged keychain fallback test starts one mock patch twice. It raises “Patch is already started” on Python 3.15.2 and 3.12.16; the merge-base reproduction confirms this predates the label change.

groups.title: Explain short IDs and address precedence
groups.kicker: Document suffix labels, short-ID input, and collision recovery
intro: The CLI reference explains why time-based prefixes collide and shows distinguishable suffixes. The reference, command help, and agent messaging skill now accept the short ID as a recipient and explain how to recover from ambiguity by using a name or full ID.

files.note: Describes suffix labels, non-UUID fallback, address precedence, and collision errors.
Updates peer discovery and send instructions for short-ID addressing.
